findings.subject: skeleton
findings.summary: Skeleton renders as a light-grey bar (rgb 240,240,240) inside any dark-scoped UIProvider, in all four themes, because --a63-skeleton-base resolves once on :root; the defect is committed as the visual baseline.
findings.evidence: Pixel measurement of apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-skeleton-themes-chromium-linux.png: dark rows bar (130,92)=(240,240,240) vs panel (520,92)=(25,25,25), 15.43:1; light rows 1.11:1. packages/styles/src/contracts/skeleton.css:10-17 sets --a63-skeleton-base only on :root; packages/styles/src/contracts/badge.css:9,52 shows the working pattern (re-declared on [data-a63-mode] scopes).
findings.fix: Emit the skeleton contract on the same mode/theme scopes as badge (fix skeleton.resolver.json and regenerate with pnpm --filter @atom63/styles generate:tokens), re-record the skeleton baselines, and add a guard (contract tokens that reference semantic tokens must be re-declared on every [data-a63-mode]/[data-a63-theme] scope) so other contracts cannot repeat it.

verified.reason: I reproduced this from the source and the baseline. skeleton.css:10-13 sets --a63-skeleton-base: var(--a63-surface-muted) only on :root. The dark block at :15-17 re-declares only the highlight, so a nested dark scope inherits the base already resolved at :root to the light surface-muted. The recipe at ui-react skeleton/skeleton.css:11 reads --a63-skeleton-base directly. In ui-react-skeleton-themes-chromium-linux.png every dark row in all four themes shows near-white bars on a dark panel. badge.css re-declares its tokens on dark scopes, so the fix pattern exists and was not applied. A clearly wrong render that is committed as the baseline meets P1.

findings.summary: In right-to-left layouts the Alert action sits on top of the title and description: the space is reserved with padding-inline-end but the action is pinned with physical right.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/alert/alert.css:51-53 (padding-inline-end reserve) vs alert.css:101-104 (position:absolute; right: var(--alert-action-inset)). check:craft physical-properties passed (sweep/craft.log) because it does not scan inset left/right. No RTL story; inferred from CSS, not rendered.
findings.fix: Use inset-inline-end for .a63-Alert-action; add an RTL story with an action to the alert baselines; extend check:craft physical-properties to flag left/right insets (also catches avatar.css:119 and empty.css:144).

verified.reason: alert.css:52-53 reserves space for the action with padding-inline-end, which falls on the left in right-to-left layouts. alert.css:101-104 pins .a63-Alert-action with physical top/right: var(--alert-action-inset), and the file has no inset-inline-end or dir override. In right-to-left the action therefore stays on the physical right, over where the title and description start, while the reserved gap sits on the left. The overlap follows directly from the CSS, though I did not render it. It breaks the system's own logical-properties rule (AGENTS.md rule 10) and right-to-left mirroring for Alert, so P1 stands.

findings.subject: load-more-trigger
findings.summary: LoadMoreTrigger creates its live region in the same render that changes its text (and mounts a new one from hidden), so 'Loading more' and 'All items loaded' are often not announced, breaking the contract's announces-loading and announces-exhausted outcomes.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/load-more-trigger/load-more-trigger.tsx:55-57 (null while hidden), 74-86 (role=status/aria-live only when state != idle); load-more-trigger.test.tsx:24-35 only checks the role after render. Not verified with a screen reader in this run.
findings.fix: Render a persistent visually-hidden role=status region in every non-hidden state (including idle) and write the message into it on state change; keep it mounted across hidden by rendering the empty region; add a test that the same live-region node persists from idle to loading to exhausted.

verified.reason: The cited code is there. load-more-trigger.tsx:55-57 returns null while hidden. Lines 74-86 add role=status and aria-live only when the state is not idle, in the same render that swaps the message text. Going from idle to loading, the live-region attributes appear at the same moment as the new text, and many screen readers miss that change. Going from hidden to loading or exhausted mounts a fresh region with its content already inside, which is the well-known pattern that often goes unannounced. Also, with the hasMore/isLoading API alone the component goes hidden when hasMore is false, so the exhausted message renders only through an explicit state prop. The contract lists announces-loading and announces-exhausted as accessibility outcomes (load-more-trigger.json:47-52), and the test only checks the role after render. I did not test it with a screen reader. The pattern is a known failure and it blocks the contract's own accessibility outcomes, so P1 holds.

findings.subject: alert
findings.summary: Every Alert, including the neutral default, is role="alert", so a persistent inline notice is announced assertively when inserted; the contract's iOS side and the docs usage both describe it as persistent.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/alert/alert.tsx:26; alert.json crossRenderer.platformAdaptations.swiftUI 'avoids assertive announcements for persistent notices'; catalog usage 'persistent inline feedback'.
findings.fix: Default to role="status" (or no live role) for default/info/success and keep role="alert" for error/warning, overridable by prop; update the conformance test at renderer-conformance.test.tsx:318-331.

findings.subject: alert
findings.summary: Alert error tone takes text and icon colour from --a63-action-danger because the status set has no error token; two token-role baseline entries record it.
findings.evidence: docs/design-system/audits/craft-baseline.json 'token-role | packages/ui-react/src/components/alert/alert.css | color: var(--a63-action-danger)': 2; alert.css:132-144; atom63 token status-error lists only info/success/warning status tokens.
findings.fix: Add --a63-status-error (+ -foreground, -subtle) to the semantic layer, alias action-danger to it where appropriate, switch alert.css error rules to it, and drop the baseline entries.

findings.subject: feedback-state
findings.summary: FeedbackState accepts a closed prop list, so consumers cannot pass id, aria-labelledby, data-* attributes or a ref to its root.
findings.fix: Extend FeedbackStateProps from React.ComponentProps<'div'> (minus title) and spread the rest onto the root.

findings.subject: feedback-state
findings.summary: FeedbackState's title is a plain div, unlike Empty's heading, so the state cannot be found by heading navigation; the error state doubles role=alert and aria-live=assertive.
findings.fix: Render the title as role=heading with a configurable level (default 3), and drop the redundant aria-live when role=alert is set.

findings.subject: feedback-state
findings.summary: FeedbackState's built-in titles, descriptions and the no-results sentence are English-only and the query sentence has no template prop.
findings.fix: Accept a messages/labels prop (or a formatter for no-results) so products can localize defaults without replacing the whole description.

findings.subject: feedback-state
findings.summary: size='page' forces min-height:100dvh and a literal 4rem padding, so inside a sheet, panel or widget on a phone it overflows its host.
findings.fix: Use min-block-size:100% (or a page-height token) and a space token; document that 'page' expects a full-height host.

findings.subject: load-more-trigger
findings.summary: The Retry action is a 14px-tall text button with no hit-area expansion, far under the 44px coarse-pointer target.
findings.fix: Render Retry as the DS Button (variant link or ghost, size sm) or add the same min-target ::after used by badge.css:272-280; use --a63-control-focus-ring-width for the outline.

findings.subject: load-more-trigger
findings.summary: LoadMoreTrigger accepts a closed prop list (no id, aria-*, data-*, style) on its sentinel.
findings.fix: Extend from React.ComponentProps<'div'> and spread the rest onto the sentinel.

findings.subject: load-more-trigger
findings.summary: Load-more parity is declared 'strict' but iOS and web differ in the idle affordance (button vs passive text), failure form (card vs inline line), variants and string overrides.
findings.fix: Either align the renderers (message/label parameters on iOS, an explicit load-more button option on web) or declare parity 'platform-adaptive' with the differences listed in platformAdaptations.

findings.subject: skeleton
findings.summary: The web shimmer always sweeps left to right, while the contract says leading-to-trailing and iOS mirrors it in RTL.
findings.fix: Add :dir(rtl) (or [dir='rtl']) keyframes that run translateX(100%) to translateX(-100%).

findings.subject: skeleton
findings.summary: Skeleton has two shallow tests and its theme baseline accepted the dark-mode defect; no reduced-motion baseline exists.
findings.fix: After the K3 fix, add a reduced-motion story/baseline and a test that dark scope changes the computed --a63-skeleton-base.

findings.subject: avatar
findings.summary: Web AvatarBadge has no way to name the status it shows, and AvatarGroupCount '+N' has no label, so status and overflow count are colour- or symbol-only for assistive tech.
findings.fix: Give AvatarBadge a required label (rendered visually hidden) and AvatarGroupCount an aria-label ('3 more'); add axe-visible stories.

findings.subject: avatar
findings.summary: The avatar status badge is pinned with physical right:0 and does not mirror in RTL; check:craft does not catch it.
findings.fix: Use inset-inline-end:0 (and inset-block-end) and add the rule to check:craft physical-properties.

findings.subject: avatar
findings.summary: The avatar contract and CLI answer say the ring is web-only, but AtomAvatar ships a ring with tests.
findings.fix: Change the adaptation to 'The square shape is web-only for now', regenerate contracts and the agent index.

findings.subject: avatar
findings.summary: AtomAvatar takes any CGFloat size and only a circle, while the contract has four sizes and two shapes with strict parity.
findings.fix: Add an AtomAvatarSize enum generated from the contract (keeping a CGFloat escape hatch if needed) and a shape parameter, or record both as platform adaptations.

findings.subject: badge
findings.summary: AtomBadge has no size or dot axis and its tone is not exposed to VoiceOver, while badge parity is 'strict'.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-ios/Sources/Atom63UI/AtomBadge.swift:13-27; badge.json crossRenderer parity 'strict', only palette declared web-only.
findings.fix: Add size (sm/md/lg) and dot to AtomBadge, expose the semantic tone via accessibilityValue, or declare the gaps as platform adaptations.

findings.subject: badge
findings.summary: badge.mdx says the palette is the Tailwind hue scale backed by --color-* tokens, but the recipe uses --a63-category-* tokens.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/badge/badge.mdx (Contract section) vs packages/ui-react/src/components/badge/badge.css:250-253; badge.json description repeats '--color-* primitives'.
findings.fix: Rewrite the palette sentences in badge.mdx and badge.json to name --a63-category-{hue} tokens; regenerate.

findings.subject: badge
findings.summary: No badge story covers long, CJK or overflowing labels, and the fixed height means a wrapped label overflows the chip.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/badge/badge.css:19; badge baselines (9) contain only short English labels.
findings.fix: Add white-space:nowrap with max-inline-size + text-overflow:ellipsis (or document wrapping), and a long/CJK story to the baselines.

findings.subject: empty
findings.summary: EmptyErrorDetail cannot be controlled and its toggle labels cannot be changed.
findings.fix: Add expanded/defaultExpanded/onExpandedChange and showLabel/hideLabel props (or a labels object).

findings.subject: empty
findings.summary: The expanded error detail (error box and copy button) has no story or baseline.
findings.fix: Add an ErrorExpanded story (defaultExpanded once K1 lands) to the visual baselines.

findings.subject: empty
findings.summary: Empty's error copy button is pinned with physical right and overlaps the start of the error text in RTL; toggle labels are English-only.
findings.fix: Use inset-inline-end; expose the labels (see the K1 finding).

findings.subject: AtomContentStateView (iOS)
findings.summary: In the error state AtomContentStateView turns the title red and draws the retry as a solid destructive button, so a recovery reads as a dangerous action and differs from web's outline retry.
findings.fix: Tint only the symbol for error, keep the title primary, and use a neutral or primary button for retry; reserve destructive for destructive actions.

findings.subject: AtomLoadMoreView (iOS)
findings.summary: AtomLoadMoreView's failure title, message and Retry label pass through AtomNotice's String init and cannot be localized; no parameter overrides any message.
findings.fix: Take LocalizedStringResource (or message parameters with defaults) for every string and pass them through.

findings.subject: AtomLoadMoreView (iOS)
findings.summary: AtomLoadMoreView posts no accessibility announcement when loading starts, fails or finishes, so VoiceOver users not focused on the row miss the change.
findings.fix: Post AccessibilityNotification.Announcement on intent changes (onChange(of: intent)).

findings.subject: animated-check
findings.summary: AnimatedCheck has no 4-theme baseline and its 300ms draw duration is a literal hidden in a TS string that check:craft cannot scan.
findings.fix: Read the duration from a --a63-motion-* token (move the CSS into animated-check.css so check:craft sees it) and add a Themes story.

findings.subject: animated-check
findings.summary: No baseline captures AnimatedCheck's reduced-motion state.
findings.fix: Add a reduced-motion story (prefers-reduced-motion emulation) to the baselines.

findings.subject: alert
findings.summary: Batch-wide: no hand-written docs page and a CLI answer that gives only an import line and boilerplate guidance; a builder cannot learn slot composition or when to choose Alert vs FeedbackState vs Empty from the docs.
findings.evidence: pnpm -s atom63 component <slug> returns summary, one usage line, two boilerplate guidance bullets ('Keep product data and fetching outside...'), an import line and the contract; no runnable snippet (atom63 example <slug> returns the Playground story). Docs page is generated from apps/docs/src/lib/component-catalog.ts; no hand-written apps/docs/src/pages/component-<slug>.mdx exists (ls apps/docs/src/pages | grep component- lists 8 others). Applies to alert, avatar, empty, feedback-state, skeleton, load-more-trigger, animated-check (badge has a stale Storybook mdx).
findings.fix: Write usage guidance and a runnable composition snippet per component in component-catalog.ts (including a 'which state component' decision table for Alert/Empty/FeedbackState/LoadMoreTrigger); regenerate the agent index.

findings.subject: feedback-state
findings.summary: FeedbackState has no crossRenderer contract although iOS offers AtomContentStateView and sync/offline states, so its 7 kinds have no declared iOS mapping.
findings.fix: Add a crossRenderer block mapping kinds to AtomContentStateView (empty/error/not-found/no-results) and AtomSyncStatusView (offline/stale), parity platform-adaptive.

findings.subject: badge
findings.summary: Badge offers both 'destructive' and 'error' (and a 'glass' alias) for overlapping meanings; the consistency lint only flags this for alert-dialog.
findings.evidence: badge.json solidVariants/semanticVariants; docs/design-system/audits/contract-consistency-baseline.json has 'status-set | alert-dialog.variants | destructive -> error' but nothing for badge.
findings.fix: Deprecate 'destructive' in favour of 'error' for Badge and extend the status-set rule to all variant lists.

findings.subject: badge
findings.summary: Interactive badges add an outer margin of (min-target - height)/2 on top of the ::after hit area, so a clickable badge takes up to 12px more space per side than a static one.
findings.fix: Drop the margin and rely on the ::after target (document the spacing needed between adjacent interactive badges).

findings.subject: alert
findings.summary: Alert inline padding is a literal 0.875rem rather than a space token.
findings.fix: Use a --a63-space-* step (3.5 if it exists, else 3) or add one.

findings.subject: AtomSkeleton (iOS)
findings.summary: AtomSkeletonRow's image placeholder is a fixed 40x40 frame that does not grow with Dynamic Type while its text lines do.
findings.fix: Use @ScaledMetric for the placeholder size.

findings.subject: badge
findings.summary: Tone is conveyed by the label text only; there is no forced-colors treatment in badge or any batch recipe (system-wide gap, see k01).
findings.evidence: grep -n forced-colors over the 8 recipes returns nothing.
findings.fix: Track with the system-wide forced-colors finding; add a forced-colors border for tonal badges and alerts.

findings.subject: alert
findings.summary: Batch-wide: none of the 8 web components has a phone-width or touch story, so narrow-width behaviour (Alert action reserve, Empty and FeedbackState centring, LoadMoreTrigger retry) is never captured.
findings.evidence: No phone or touch story: grep -il 'phone|viewport|mobile' over the 8 batch story files returns nothing.
findings.fix: Add a Phone story (viewport 375, coarse pointer) to alert, empty, feedback-state and load-more-trigger and include them in the visual baselines.

findings.subject: AtomNotice (iOS)
findings.summary: Batch-wide iOS: the six SwiftUI counterparts have no reference docs beyond the CLI's 'Web and iOS' contract section and the demo catalog.
findings.evidence: iOS reference is only the CLI 'Web and iOS' section and the demo catalog (examples/ios-demo/Atom63Demo/CatalogRegistry.swift); no DocC or docs page.
findings.fix: Add DocC comments with a usage snippet to each public initializer and surface them in atom63 component <slug> under the iOS heading.
